key_concepts: Continents were once joined in a supercontinent called Pangaea.
Pangaea later broke apart and continents moved to their present positions.
Tectonic plates have spread and changed Earth's surface over geologic time.
Continental coastlines can be matched like puzzle pieces.
Biological evidence such as fossils supports continental drift.
Geological evidence such as matching rock formations supports continental drift.
Climate evidence supports the past existence of Pangaea.
Seafloor spreading provides evidence for plate movement.
Maps and diagrams can illustrate the past positions of continents.
